Menu About Blog Search for: Center Street Electronics Written By: Chuck Stark Center Street Electronics is relatively new to the effects market. With John Hadl and Jason Brown at the helm, C.S.E has been building custom effects pedals for the last two years and officially opened C.S.E up for business January 1st 2014. It started with the curiosity of Jason modding pedals which brought John down the path to building custom effects. They started with a clone of the Way Huge Red Llama (excellent choice) and the TS808. These clones developed into the Godly Red and The Murphy and so it began! They have three pedals (videos will be below :D), Rasputin Fuzz – $149.99 – 1 volume knob, 1 fuzz knob and two dark/bright switches The Murphy – $149.99 – 1 drive knob, 1 tone knob, 1 level knob Godly Red – $149.99 – 1 gain knob, 1 volume knob, 1 god switch C.S.E is rolling out two new pedals. A simple, one knob fuzz in the Druid Fuzz for $99.99, and a reverb pedal based around the Box of Hall reverb circuit for $149.99. Overall, these pedals are simple, hand-made boxes of rock. The most impressive feature of C.S.E is that they do more than the pedal line that they have created. They do Custom Shop work building custom pedals form your ideas, and they also do pedal and amp mods! So my advice to you is to have them mod out your pedal board and add a few of theirs to it for a totally custom board. They are also hosting a giveaway on their facebook page. They will be giving away a free pedal each month for the rest of the year. Be sure to check them out, like their page, and trade them your money for some sweet ass tones. Facebook – https://www.facebook.com/centerstreetelectronics Website – http://www.centerstreetelectronics.com/ Posted in Uncategorized on April 13, 2014 by The Notorious Note . Leave a comment Are you a Way Huge, Way Huge Fan? Written By: Chuck Stark Before we get into some of the fun stuff, a history lesson from Dunlop. Launched in 1992 by Jeorge Tripps, Way Huge Electronics quickly created a buzz among southern California guitar players and began to define the boutique effects market. In late 1999 with 15 models, the company closed its doors as Tripps pursued other opportunities to hone his skills as a designer. As Way Huge exited from the market, the demand for the products soared, driving online auctions well into the hundreds, sometimes thousands of dollars. In 2006, Dunlop welcomed Tripps and Way Huge into the family. Finally, Tripps was able to make Way Huge Electronics the way he had always envisioned, with a dedicated design team and production facility at his fingertips. Since then, Dunlop has helped Way Huge Electronics bring their hot-rodded vintage tones to the mass market at an affordable price. I’ve been using the Way Huge Green Rhino and it is absolutely amazing. The Mk II has the classic overdrive that you crave but has evolved to include cool new features that make it even better. In addition to the Volume, Tone, and Drive controls, you get a 100Hz EQ knob to cut or boost your low end by 12dB. This pedal can drive any amp into a sweet sensation. Along with the a Green Rhino, I’ve been using the Aqua Puss Delay. I saw it on the boards of John Mayer and Brad Paisley so I figured it would be worth a shot to try. I was amazed with the simplicity, and clarity of the pedal. Its delay ranges from 20ms to 300ms. It also includes a feedback knob and a blend for your signal. Be sure to check out the whole Way Huge line at http://www.jimdunlop.com/products/electronics/way-huge-electronics Enjoy these demos, share some of your own?
